persona: Relaxed and brief. Calls his home policy 'contents insurance' out of habit. Made one earlier claim this year, for a stolen bike.
initial_message: Hi there, I'd like to claim on my contents insurance please. The hailstorm on Tuesday 1 September cracked the skylight in our bathroom ceiling. A glazier has put a cover over it for now.

facts.policyholder.name: Oliver Cedarholt
facts.incident.description: During a hailstorm on Tuesday evening large hail cracked the acrylic dome of the skylight above our bathroom. A little water dripped into the skylight shaft. A glazier put a temporary cover over it the next morning.
facts.loss.description: Skylight dome above the bathroom cracked in a star pattern; small water mark in the skylight shaft
facts.mitigation.temporary_repair: Karaka Worth Glazing fitted a temporary cover over the skylight on Wednesday 2 September 2026
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the cracked skylight from inside the bathroom. Available now.
facts.evidence.attendance_note: The glazier's attendance note. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Karaka Worth Glazing, total $1,610.00 including GST, dated 4 September 2026. Available now.
facts.if_asked_which_policy: It is the policy for the house, NW-SYN-HOM-200013. I always mix up the names.
facts.if_asked_about_previous_claims: One. I claimed for a stolen mountain bike in January this year.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo looking straight up at a square skylight in a white bathroom ceiling on an overcast evening. The clear acrylic dome of the skylight has a star-shaped crack with several long fractures running from the centre, and a few white hailstones rest on top of the dome. The skylight shaft is lined with white plasterboard with a small water mark on one side. Only the skylight and the ceiling around it are in the frame.
materials.purpose: Shows the hail damage to the skylight

reasons: CTL-H-013/photo-skylight.jpg: image-only pass names 'window pane', expected one of ['skylight', 'skylight dome', 'dome', 'roof window', 'roof light']

data.found: Acrylic skylight dome above the bathroom cracked by hail. Minor water entry into the skylight shaft.
data.work_done: Fitted a temporary polythene cover over the dome and taped the edges. No further water entry.
data.follow_up: Replace the skylight dome and reseal the flashing.

materials.purpose: Contractor record of the emergency work

materials.purpose: Policy schedule that matches the home wording in the knowledge base

design.notes: Innocent control: the account has exactly one other submitted claim in the past year (contents, incident 17 January 2026, submitted 19 January 2026), a different event; two are needed for the indicator. The claimant says 'contents insurance', but the skylight is part of the house, so the Claim must end as home (G3).

triage.rationale: Hail damage to a skylight at the insured address, nobody hurt, temporary cover in place, photo and a complete quote (NZD 1,610.00 including GST), policy on file. One earlier claim in the past year is below the two the indicator needs. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

prior_claims_12m.basis: Exactly one other submitted claim in the past year (contents, submitted 2026-01-19); two are needed

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 March 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-03-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

possible_duplicate.basis: The earlier claim is a different family (contents) and months earlier
